incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD#12345 fired — p99 latency > 3.0s (5m window) for route /v1/generate (eu-west), severity: page. Notified: @alex (oncall)

alex (oncall): acking. seeing a sawtooth on p99, p95 is okay. grabbing logs + timeline.

alex (oncall): quick check — any deploys in last 10m? @jamie?

jamie (product): no prod deploys in last 30m, nothing on release board. We did push a config change to autoscaler yesterday but rolls finished earlier.

alex (oncall): ok. running quick tail: ```kubectl logs -n inference svc-inference-eu --since=15m | grep "latency" | tail -n 50``` seeing a cluster of slow responses from a subset of pods, ~3 of 12.

maria (sre): looks like sidecar mempressure on those hosts, oom_kill from model-loader? Getting `nvml` warnings in host dmesg. Can you paste pod names?

alex (oncall): pods: inference-eu-7f4db, inference-eu-7f4dc, inference-eu-7f4dd. cpu spike then long GC pauses in runtime logs. Also noticed repeated `kv-cache-miss` for those pod IDs.

maria (sre): hmm kv-cache miss pattern could explain p99 tail. If a hotpath lost its prefix cache we get regen. I'm going to check autoscaler and eviction: `kubectl describe hpa/batcher-eu` and host eviction events.

pd-bot: PagerDuty PD#12345 — acknowledged by alex (oncall). Escalation timer paused.

alex (oncall): WIP: restarting the three affected pods to warm KV cache and release mem hold. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-eu --field-selector=metadata.name=inference-eu-7f4db,inference-eu-7f4dc,inference-eu-7f4dd` (manual targeted restarts).

jamie (product): flagging potential customer impact: user-facing latencies on embeddings endpoints for EU customers. Suggest immediate status note if customer-facing errors spike.

maria (sre): I see core-dump on one host and host-level memory reclaim. I'll cordon the node hosting those pods and move load. `kubectl cordon node/eu-23` then drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`.

alex (oncall): pods restarted, watching metrics. p99 dropping from 3.2s -> 1.1s after warmups on two pods, third pod still spiky.

maria (sre): draining node now. also increasing sidecar JVM heap on the group to avoid GC thrash — applying a transient config bump to 1.2x. Pushing change to canary subset of eu replicas.

jamie (product): ok please keep me posted on customer-visible metrics (latency by org). I'll hold off on a public status until we have sustained improvement 30m.

alex (oncall): telemetry shows p99 back at ~900ms cluster-wide after drain. PD auto-resolve threshold will fire if sustained.

pd-bot: PagerDuty PD#12345 — resolved (auto) after 20m; triggered by decrease in p99 metric.

maria (sre): root cause hypothesis: a combination of host memory reclaim + localized KV cache eviction caused regeneration pressure on a subset of replicas, producing tail latency. Follow-ups: 1) tune sidecar heap and OOM thresholds 2) improve node autoscale to avoid evictions during bursts 3) add targeted KV cache warmup after restart 4) add alerting for host-level reclaim spikes so we get earlier signals.

alex (oncall): filing a short incident note and a ticket for follow-ups. tagging infra and runtime teams. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jamie (product): noted — I'll schedule a customer impact review if we see related org-level latency regressions in the next 24h.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed by alex (oncall).
